setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major through the test MIDI device. The channel range is steps 1-4, the tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Lock all to pentatonic is Off. Lock all to pentatonic forces every note you play onto a five-note subset of the chosen scale, so each scale step below changes which five notes survive.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor (5,8), which starts on the trig page. Tap steps 5, 6 and 7 on the trig row, (5,4), (6,4) and (7,4). Press (5,8) again for the note page and press the rising diagonal (1,7), (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2), (7,1): one note per step, scale degrees I-VII, C D E F G A B. The note page now shows a rising diagonal.
steps.title: Extend the pattern to seven steps

steps.caption: Press (5,8) for the velocity page and tap (5,1), (6,2) and (7,3): the velocity bars for steps 5, 6 and 7 light up.
steps.title: Set the velocities of steps 5 to 7

steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8), hold step 1 (1,4) and tap step 7 (7,4). Steps 1 to 7 light up and step 8 stays dark, so the channel range is steps 1-7.
steps.title: Set the range to seven steps

steps.caption: Press Play and listen to two loops with Lock all to pentatonic at its default Off: all seven plain C major degrees sound, 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71.
steps.title: Hear the plain major scale

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, scroll to Lock all to pentatonic and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.
steps.title: Turn Lock all to pentatonic on

steps.caption: Scroll down to Lock random to pent. and turn E3 left to Off, then do the same for Lock merged to pent. Both rows read Off, so Lock all to pentatonic is the only option that can change a pitch.
steps.title: Switch off the other two locks

steps.caption: Press K2 to step back, then K1 to close the menu, and play the seven steps again: 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 69, 72. Major keeps degrees 1/2/3/5/6 (C D E G A). F falls to E and B rises to C because only those five are allowed.
steps.title: Snap major to pentatonic

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent and press K3. The Scale row reads Harmonic Major.
steps.title: Pick Harmonic Major

steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Harmonic Major keeps the same degrees as Major, 1/2/3/5/6, but its sixth is A-flat: 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 68, 72. F falls to E, A-flat stays and B rises to C.
steps.title: Step to Harmonic Major

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Minor and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. The minor family keeps degrees 1/3/4/5/7 (C E-flat F G B-flat): 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 70. D snaps up to E-flat and A-flat snaps down to G.
steps.title: Minor uses its own five notes

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Harmonic Minor and press K3, return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play. Then open the Scale Editor again, turn E3 one more detent and press K3: the Scale row reads Melodic Minor.
steps.title: Pick Harmonic Minor, then Melodic Minor

steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Harmonic Minor and Melodic Minor give the same pitches: 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 71. Only the top note differs from Minor, B-flat becoming B. In Harmonic Minor A-flat snaps down to G; in Melodic Minor A sits exactly between G and B, and an equal-distance note snaps to the lower pitch, so it also lands on G.
steps.title: Hear Harmonic and Melodic Minor

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Dorian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Dorian keeps degrees 1/2/4/5/7 (C D F G B-flat): 60, 62, 62, 65, 67, 70, 70. E-flat falls to D and A rises to B-flat.
steps.title: Step to Dorian

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Phrygian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Phrygian keeps degrees 1/3/4/6/7 (C E-flat F A-flat B-flat): 60, 60, 63, 65, 68, 68, 70. D-flat falls to C and G rises to A-flat.
steps.title: Step to Phrygian

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Lydian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Lydian keeps degrees 2/3/5/6/7 (D E G A B), so the tonic C snaps down to the B below it: 59, 62, 64, 67, 67, 69, 71.
steps.title: See the lower boundary snap

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Mixolydian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Mixolydian keeps degrees 1/2/4/5/6 (C D F G A): 60, 62, 65, 65, 67, 69, 69. E rises to F and B-flat falls to A.
steps.title: Step to Mixolydian

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Locrian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Locrian keeps degrees 2/3/4/6/7 (D-flat E-flat F A-flat B-flat), so the tonic C snaps up to D-flat and G-flat snaps down to F: 61, 61, 63, 65, 65, 68, 70.
steps.title: Step to Locrian

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, scroll to Lock all to pentatonic and turn E3 left to Off. The row reads Off.
steps.title: Turn Lock all to pentatonic off

steps.caption: Close the menu and play. All seven plain Locrian pitches return: 60, 61, 63, 65, 66, 68, 70. Musical tip: leave Lock all to pentatonic On when a pattern is random or generative, so every note lands in a five-note set that stays consonant in any scale, and Off when you want the full seven-note colour.
steps.title: All seven Locrian pitches return

title: Restrict every note to five degrees
